content.text: Created a Work In Progress (WIP) PR:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1262

As there are other issues dependent on this, I have pushed the work I have done so far to the above branch so that someone else can work on this, if necessary. I will try to continue on this next weekend if this is still incomplete.
Thanks for making your progress available,
I have a question about this. I am wondering if there is a use case for providing a Memento-Datetime without a Body and vice versa?
I can see either:
1. you POST to the LDPCv and get a new Memento created from the current resource with the current datetime
2. you POST to the LDPCv with a Memento-Datetime header and a body to create a version for the specified date and the specified content.
I'm not clear on a use case for creating a version of the current resource body but with a different date and/or creating a version with a different body but the current datetime.
Does that make sense?
In addition to your 1. and 2. use cases, the other use case that we should support is:
3. you POST to the LDPCv with a Memento-Datetime header and an EMPTY body to create an EMPTY version for the specified date and the specified content.
Actually, this is probably better numbered as 2b. since it is an example usage of 2.
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1296
Resolved by
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/9630a378158d64459788fa469c17544f71c5c620
Update POST to LDPCv to include support for versioning headers.  In practice, the LDPCv for object with uri <
http://localhost/rest/a
> would be <
http://localhost/rest/a/fcr:versions
See:
https://fcrepo.github.io/fcrepo-specification/#ldpcvpost
if the request contained a body, then a new LDPRm is created from the submitted body
if the request body was empty, then a new LDPRm is created from the current version of the LDPRv.
If a Memento-Datetime header is provided as part of this POST request, then the newly created LDPRm must attempt to use it as the memento datetime
If a LDPRm already exists with the same Memento-Datetime specified, then the LDPRm is not created and a '412 already exists' response is returned.
Response from a successful creation should return a LDPRm headers, particularly the Memento-Datetime of the new LDPRm.
Response must include a Location header referencing the URI of the newly created LDPRm.
